request.text:
representing number is an actual credence. Several results named in
this chapter are reported but not proved here. Their primary sources,
as the chapter's reference list identifies them
\parencite[pp.~249--251]{HajekStaffel2021Dynamics}, form the following
finite set. Savage's representation theorem: L.~J. Savage,
\emph{The Foundations of Statistics} (New York: Wiley, 1954). Jeffrey's
alternative axioms and Bolker's representation theorem, which the
authors report as cited by Jeffrey and for which they give no separate
reference: R.~C. Jeffrey, \emph{The Logic of Decision} (Chicago:
University of Chicago Press, 1965). The Dutch-book theorem attributed to
Ramsey and de Finetti: F.~P. Ramsey, ``Truth and probability'' (1926
manuscript), in D.~H. Mellor (ed.), \emph{Philosophical Papers}
(Cambridge University Press, 1990), pp.~52--94; and B. de Finetti,
``Foresight: its logical laws, its subjective sources'' (French
original 1937), in H.~E. Kyburg and H.~E. Smokler (eds.),
\emph{Studies in Subjective Probability} (New York: Wiley, 1964),
pp.~100--110. Its converse: J.~G. Kemeny, ``Fair bets and inductive
probabilities'', \emph{Journal of Symbolic Logic} 20(3) (1955),
263--273. The general distance characterizations of conditioning and
Jeffrey conditioning: P. Diaconis and S. Zabell, ``Updating subjective
probability'', \emph{Journal of the American Statistical Association}
77(380) (1982), 822--830; the finite-partition cases are
\cref{thm:p15-rat41-minimal-update}. The results on approximate
coherence: G. De Bona and J. Staffel, ``Graded incoherence for
accuracy-firsters'', \emph{Philosophy of Science} 84(2) (2017),
189--213, and ``Why be (approximately) coherent?'', \emph{Analysis}
78(3) (2018), 405--415, with the earlier treatments the authors cite,
M.~J. Schervish, T. Seidenfeld and J.~B. Kadane, ``Measuring
incoherence'', \emph{Sankhy\=a} 64 (2002), 561--587, and L. Zynda,
``Coherence as an ideal of rationality'', \emph{Synthese} 109(2)
(1996), 175--216. No theorem proved in this chapter uses any of these
reported results as a premise.
request.reason: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-1-C05: the assessment found no explicit finite dependent-source set for the surveyed results left unproved (Savage/Bolker, de Finetti/Kemeny, Diaconis-Zabell, De Bona-Staffel). Bibliographic data are taken from the held chapter's reference list, read in source/references/p15-rationality-4-1/hajek-staffel-2021-publisher.pdf: De Bona-Staffel 2017/2018, de Finetti 1964, Diaconis-Zabell 1982 and Jeffrey 1965 on p. 249; Kemeny 1955, Ramsey 1990, Savage 1954 and Schervish-Seidenfeld-Kadane 2002 on p. 250; Zynda 1996 on p. 251. Bolker has no entry in that list (p. 241 says only 'cited by Jeffrey'). None of these works is held; the text therefore identifies them and does not present their content. The final sentence should be checked by the owner against the chapter's theorem premises before merge.

In entropy terms, each of the three uniform priors is the unconstrained
maximum-entropy law only relative to Lebesgue measure in its own
coordinate. \Cref{thm:p15-w02b-p15-042-power-coordinates} computes the
continuous entropy of each prior in each of the three coordinates, and the
comparison in \cref{sec:p15-w02b-p15-042-relationships} tabulates the
values; the computation makes the conflict exact and does not choose a
privileged coordinate.

request.text:
such as Dempster--Shafer, ranking, belief-revision, and possibility
frameworks. These are not interchangeable versions of ratio conditioning,
and the handbook treats each with its own representation and change rule.
Dempster--Shafer belief and plausibility functions are defined in
\cref{def:p15-r47-mass} (\cref{sec:p15-r47-evidence}), and conditioning a
lower prevision on an observed event is \cref{sec:p15-ip-conditioning}.
Ranking functions and their revision are \cref{sec:p15-rationality-5-3};
the finite bridge from negative ranks to possibility and necessity measures
is \cref{def:p15-r47-ranking,thm:p15-r47-ranking}, and possibilistic belief
statements are \cref{sec:p15-r47-modal}. AGM revision of a deductively
closed belief set is \cref{def:p08-agm}, with its faithful-preorder
representation in \cref{thm:p08-agm-representation}; ranked models and
rational closure for defeasible conditionals are
\cref{sec:p08-ranked-models-rational-closure}. None of these change rules
is the ratio formula applied to different numbers.
